title: Before 1776: Life in the American Colonies
description:
S01 E02 — Spain's New World Empire
A newly united Spain accidentally finds itself in possession of previously unknown lands; how Spain sets about exploiting the New World; how it acquires the mineral wealth of Mexico, which excites the ambitions of other European powers.

title: Before 1776: Life in the American Colonies
description:
S01 E03 — John Smith, Pocahontas, and Jamestown
Investigating the varied life of Captain John Smith; after a career as a mercenary fighting Turks, he is assigned to the London Company's venture to Virginia; there, he helps found Jamestown; his story of being saved by Pocahontas may be fabricated.

title: Before 1776: Life in the American Colonies
description:
S01 E04 — Virginia and the Chesapeake after Smith
How tobacco seeds from South America rescue the Virginia colony from extinction but also cause increase conflict with Native Americans; Virginia remains a death trap for Europeans, which leads to a greater reliance on slave labor.

title: Before 1776: Life in the American Colonies
description:
S01 E05 — The Pilgrims and Plymouth
Who the pilgrims are; how this small devout religious community revolutionizes the colonization of North America; how a crisis aboard the Mayflower prompts the Mayflower Compact, which asserts a principle claimed by no other colony in the New World.

title: Before 1776: Life in the American Colonies
description:
S01 E06 — The Iroquois, the French, and the Dutch
Expansion by the Dutch and the French brings them into contact with the Iroquois, the most powerful people in eastern North America; how the goals and principles of these three peoples collide as they compete for pelts and power.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E01 — Native America: A Story of Survival
The commonly held views of Native Americans and the realities of a tapestry of vibrant cultures; Cobb explains the pitfalls that occur when history does not provide this crucial viewpoint; the mistake of consigning Native Americans to the past.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The Columbian Exchange: New Worlds for All
The misleading dichotomy of Old World and New World impacts perceptions of Native Americans; the Columbian Exchange is the crux behind the creation of new worlds for all; shaping everything from the fauna and flora to the cuisines of the world.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E03 — The Native South and Southwest in the 1600s
The cultures that exist before the Spanish Invasion; the struggle for power through Hernando de Soto's entrada through the Southeast; the Pueblo War for Independence in the Southwest; the Native American worlds born in the aftermath of these events.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E04 — Werowocomoco and Montaup in the 1600s
How connections are forged between Native Americans and newcomers as they incorporate each other into their worlds; examples across the Northeastern Woodlands down to Werowocomoco; how the search for common ground begins at first contact.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E05 — Iroquoia and Wendake in the 1600s
Once Europeans arrive, the Native peoples of the Northeast want to maintain their autonomy; the strategies and experiences of the Wendat and Iroquois; Native Americans transform the European colonial project while preserving a measured separatism.

title: Understanding Greek and Roman Technology: From Catapult to the Pantheon
description:
S01 E01 — Technology in the Classical World
An exploration of ancient Greek and Roman engineering; the technological edge that allows the Greeks to beat the Persians at the Battle of Salamis; a preview of an important piece of technology.

title: Understanding Greek and Roman Technology: From Catapult to the Pantheon
description:
S01 E02 — The Substance of Technology - Materials
The engineering materials available in classical antiquity; the simple physics of compression and tension; considering stone, wood, clay, copper, bronze and iron; the influence of their use and properties on technological systems.

title: Understanding Greek and Roman Technology: From Catapult to the Pantheon
description:
S01 E03 — From Quarry to Temple - Building in Stone
The journey of an important construction material; following a block of stone from a quarry to its final resting place in the wall of a Greek temple; how stone blocks are extracted from solid bedrock, moved many miles, and then fitted together.

title: Understanding Greek and Roman Technology: From Catapult to the Pantheon
description:
S01 E04 — Stone Masonry Perfected - The Greek Temple
A classical-era temple; the achievements of Hellenic civilization; its origins; its architectural consistency; the principles of Greek temple design; its structural limitations.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E01 — Dawn of the Roman Empire
Setting the stage for Rome's transition from a republic to an empire; Octavian wins a civil war against Mark Antony; he soon achieves what Julius Caesar could not, a one-man rule over Rome.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E02 — Augustus, the First Emperor
Meeting Octavian, who becomes Rome's first emperor; he takes the title of Augustus; gaining control of the military; ruling Rome without inspiring his own assassination; how these are some of history's most astonishing feats.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E03 — Tiberius and Caligula
Despite his achievements, Augustus fails in the key area of choosing a successor; after an almost comical series of events, he secures a male heir to take the throne; witnessing the debacle of Roman leadership under Tiberius and Caligula.

title: The Roman Empire: From Augustus to the Fall of Rome
description:
S01 E04 — Claudius and Nero
The succession after Caligula continues to be a problem for the Roman Empire; Claudius, though physically challenged, is a good administrator; Nero is depraved and self-aggrandizing, nearly bankrupting the empire; tracing the story of their rule.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Rethinking the Persian Empire
Cyrus, Darius and Xerxes; these Persian kings are sometimes stereotyped as one-dimensional despots in Greek histories; the truth about the Achaemenid Persian Empire; an empire that stretches from Egypt and Asia Minor, all the way to the Indus Valley.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E02 — Questioning the Sources
Greek historians provide valuable information about the Persian Empire; the Greek perspective is often negatively biased; archaeology uncovers inscriptions, administrative tablets and other documents that let the Persians speak for themselves.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E03 — The World before Cyrus
The ancient world before the Persian Empire; in the centuries leading up to the Persian Empire, the Assyrians are the major international power; the Assyrian kingdom collapses; it leaves a power vacuum in the region; the stage set for new power.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E04 — Cyrus and Cambyses - Founders of the Empire
Cyrus, the first great king of the Persian Empire, expands the empire through pragmatic leadership; he uses local customs and traditions and thereby gains legitimacy over Central Asia and Babylon; his son Cambyses expands the empire into Egypt.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description: Eastern civilization has a fascinating story with important consequences; the accomplishments of Eastern civilization, from the material economy of day-to-day life to the political and religious philosophies that bind Eastern cultures together.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E02 — Yin and Yang - The Geography of China
Starting with the geography and climate of China, the cradle of Eastern civilization; looking at the geographical regions of China; exploring the country's two great river systems, which divide Chinese culture into two distinct regions.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E03 — Early China and the Mysterious Xia
The beginnings of Chinese history; what archeological evidence shows about humans in the Paleolithic and Neolithic eras; looking at the fragmented cultures of early civilizations, including the mysterious Xia dynasty.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E04 — The Coming of the Shang
Looking at evidence that the Shang dynasty is responsible for the development of Chinese writing, a complex social structure and the first large cities in East Asia; visiting the cities and tombs of the first significant Chinese dynasty.

title: London: A Short History of the Greatest City in the Western World
description:
S01 E01 — There's No Place like London
Giving a brief overview of London; introducing several overarching themes; London's growth, diversity and resilience; showing why this magnificent metropolis is the greatest city in the Western world.

title: London: A Short History of the Greatest City in the Western World
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise and Fall of Roman Londinium
Exploring the early centuries of London's history; its foundation in 60 C.E. as Londinium, the largest Roman settlement in Britain; its eventual decline and abandonment at the end of the 4th century C.E. after the collapse of the Roman Empire.

title: London: A Short History of the Greatest City in the Western World
description:
S01 E03 — Medieval London's Thousand-Year Climb
Knowing how London revives itself and plays a prominent part in early British history; discovering the important roles played by the Christian church, Viking scourges, leaders such as Alfred the Great and William the Conqueror; the Magna Carta.

title: London: A Short History of the Greatest City in the Western World
description:
S01 E04 — Economic Life in Chaucer's London
The streets of medieval London as it is lived and experienced by Geoffrey Chaucer; this historical tour includes looks at places such as the Tower of London, the London docks, the markets on East Cheap and the shops and taverns of Cheapside.

title: London: A Short History of the Greatest City in the Western World
description:
S01 E05 — Politics and Religion in Chaucer's London
Touring 14th-century London by heading west and exploring the importance of London's Guildhall (City Hall); the magnificence of old St. Paul's Cathedral (as well as its churchyard); the excitement of the Strand; the splendor of Westminster Abbey.

title: London: A Short History of the Greatest City in the Western World
description:
S01 E06 — London Embraces the Early Tudors
Investigating the impact of the Tudor dynasty on the lives of Londoners; pointed looks at the reigns of Henry VII, Henry VIII and Mary I; studying how London deals with the religious turmoil brought about by the Protestant Reformation.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E01 — From Jesus to the Creation of the Church
In the early days of the Christian faith, there is no church; no single institution to guide the followers of Jesus; stepping into the world of the early church; the roots of Christianity as found in ancient Jewish traditions and the gospel.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E02 — The First Christian Institutions
In the first century A.D., the followers of Christ evolve from a band of disciples into tight-knit communities of worship; a glimpse of these communities in some of the earliest Christian documents; the Acts of the Apostles and the letters of Paul.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E03 — Christianities in the Early Church
Christianity quickly spreads all over the Mediterranean region in the first few centuries; learning how believers adapt the practice of their faith to create a great diversity of worship in the early church.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E04 — Persecution and Saints
The Christian church catches the attention of the Roman emperor; he views the faithful as a threat to imperial authority and Roman culture; the widespread persecution of Christians that follows; a new class of Christian heroes, the martyred saints.

title: The Catholic Church: A History
description:
S01 E05 — Peace between Empire and Church
In 312 A.D., Christianity gains a powerful ally when the Roman emperor Constantine adopts the faith of Jesus as his own; seeing how this shift affects Christian believers; the church goes from being a persecuted minority to a privileged minority.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E01 — A Meditation on Empire
What makes a true "empire"; how empires rise and flourish; how they decline and fall; discovering pointed answers to these and other fundamental questions about the study of empires.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E02 — Lands, Seas, and Sources
The geography of the ancient Near East plays a decisive role in the region's fascinating empires; looking at the kinds of archeological and documentary evidence like discoveries from excavations of ancient sites help in understanding the period.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E03 — Sargon and the Dawn of Empire
Charting the rise and the eventual fall of the Akkadian Empire, established by Sargon and strengthened by his grandson, Naram-Sin; learning how they forged the administrative pattern that future Mesopotamian empires follow, pivoting the king.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E04 — The Third Dynasty of Ur
Professor Dise discusses the brief rise and the eventual disintegration of the imperial dynasty of Ur III in Sumer in the late 22nd century B.C., analyzing how the dynasty's ruler Ur-Nammu introduced tyrannical taxes and economic systems.

title: Ancient Empires before Alexander
description:
S01 E05 — The Empire of Hammurabi
King Hammurabi fills in the power vacuum left in Mesopotamia after Ur III; establishing the First Dynasty of Babylon, he administers rule through a detailed code of law; the First Dynasty swiftly collapses after Hammurabi's death.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E01 — Rome: The Eternal City
Visiting the sites along the Tiber River, which tell Rome's story; climbing the Monte Caprino, one of Rome's seven hills, to see sculptures, Michelangelo's magnificent piazza, and palaces; exploring the artworks of the Church of the Aracoeli.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E02 — The Capitoline and the Colosseum
Visiting the Piazza Venezia, known for its Renaissance and Baroque palaces, famous talking statues and the church of Santa Maria di Loreto; exploring the imposing forums of Trajan and Augustus and the history and lore of Rome's iconic Colosseum.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E03 — Imperial Palaces of the Palatine Hill
Learning about the marvels of Roman hydraulic engineering and visiting the massive Circus Maximus; exploring the ruined baths; discovering the palace complex of Domitian, the houses of Augustus and Livia and the Renaissance Farnese Gardens.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E04 — Pompeii: A City Frozen in Time
Visiting the preserved city of Pompeii, with its view into the lives of Roman citizens; envisioning the grandeur of Pompeii's forum; exploring mansions and bakeries; stopping at the theater and arena; visiting the Villa of Mysteries.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E05 — The Roman Forum
Learning about the history of the epicenter of Rome's empire; visiting key sites of the forum, including the Temple of Venus and Roma; stopping at the Basilica of Maxentius and Constantine and the House and Temple of the Vestal Virgins.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E01 — Paleolithic Cave Art of Spain and France
The oldest paintings in the world, in the extraordinary cave art of Altamira, Lascaux, and Chauvet.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E02 — The Taj Mahal of Agra
Learning about the builder of Taj, the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, for whom it was built.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E03 — Australia's Great Barrier Reef
The Great Barrier Reef is one of the world's natural wonders, drawing travelers to its shimmering, multicolored coral reefs, teeming with fascinating marine life.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E04 — The Mogao Grottoes and Manuscripts
The Mogao Grottoes, dug out of cliffs in the desert of northwestern China, contain one of the most dazzling collections of Buddhist art in the world.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E05 — Persepolis, the Great Persian Capital
The citadel of Persepolis was the capital of the Achaemenid Empire for nearly 200 years.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E06 — Easter Island and the Moai
The moai, the colossal statues of Easter Island, are a testament to human innovation.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E01 — Pacific Crest Trail
Exploring the Pacific Crest Trail, an extraordinary route that stretches 2,650 miles from the deserts of Southern California on the Mexico border all the way to the Canadian border in Washington.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E02 — Hayduke Trail
Mick journeys along the hazardous 800-mile backcountry route of the Hayduke Trail.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E03 — Pacific Northwest Trail
Traveling one of the most scenic and rugged long-distance trails in the world: the 1,200-mile Pacific Northwest Trail.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E04 — Continental Divide Trail
At 3,100 miles, the Continental Divide Trail is the second-longest National Scenic Trail in the United States, and arguably the most rugged, remote, and hazardous of them all.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E05 — Great Allegheny Passage
Exploring a predominantly flat hiking trail from Pennsylvania's Pittsburgh to Maryland's Cumberland.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E01 — Rome: The Eternal City
Visiting the sites along the Tiber River, which tell Rome's story; climbing the Monte Caprino, one of Rome's seven hills, to see sculptures, Michelangelo's magnificent piazza, and palaces; exploring the artworks of the Church of the Aracoeli.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E02 — The Capitoline and the Colosseum
Visiting the Piazza Venezia, known for its Renaissance and Baroque palaces, famous talking statues and the church of Santa Maria di Loreto; exploring the imposing forums of Trajan and Augustus and the history and lore of Rome's iconic Colosseum.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E03 — Imperial Palaces of the Palatine Hill
Learning about the marvels of Roman hydraulic engineering and visiting the massive Circus Maximus; exploring the ruined baths; discovering the palace complex of Domitian, the houses of Augustus and Livia and the Renaissance Farnese Gardens.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E04 — Pompeii: A City Frozen in Time
Visiting the preserved city of Pompeii, with its view into the lives of Roman citizens; envisioning the grandeur of Pompeii's forum; exploring mansions and bakeries; stopping at the theater and arena; visiting the Villa of Mysteries.

title: The Guide to Essential Italy
description:
S01 E05 — The Roman Forum
Learning about the history of the epicenter of Rome's empire; visiting key sites of the forum, including the Temple of Venus and Roma; stopping at the Basilica of Maxentius and Constantine and the House and Temple of the Vestal Virgins.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E01 — Paleolithic Cave Art of Spain and France
The oldest paintings in the world, in the extraordinary cave art of Altamira, Lascaux, and Chauvet.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E02 — The Taj Mahal of Agra
Learning about the builder of Taj, the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, for whom it was built.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E03 — Australia's Great Barrier Reef
The Great Barrier Reef is one of the world's natural wonders, drawing travelers to its shimmering, multicolored coral reefs, teeming with fascinating marine life.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E04 — The Mogao Grottoes and Manuscripts
The Mogao Grottoes, dug out of cliffs in the desert of northwestern China, contain one of the most dazzling collections of Buddhist art in the world.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E05 — Persepolis, the Great Persian Capital
The citadel of Persepolis was the capital of the Achaemenid Empire for nearly 200 years.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E06 — Easter Island and the Moai
The moai, the colossal statues of Easter Island, are a testament to human innovation.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E01 — Pacific Crest Trail
Exploring the Pacific Crest Trail, an extraordinary route that stretches 2,650 miles from the deserts of Southern California on the Mexico border all the way to the Canadian border in Washington.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E02 — Hayduke Trail
Mick journeys along the hazardous 800-mile backcountry route of the Hayduke Trail.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E03 — Pacific Northwest Trail
Traveling one of the most scenic and rugged long-distance trails in the world: the 1,200-mile Pacific Northwest Trail.

title: America's Great Trails
description:
S01 E04 — Continental Divide Trail
At 3,100 miles, the Continental Divide Trail is the second-longest National Scenic Trail in the United States, and arguably the most rugged, remote, and hazardous of them all.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E01 — The World of Genesis
Considering the nature and scope of biblical archeology; how the Book of Genesis makes its case for the existence of a single God; archeological evidence for a great flood in ancient times; its possible connection to the biblical story of Noah.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E02 — The Tower of Babel
The symbolism of the tower and pyramid in ancient architecture; the Egyptian step pyramid at Saqqara; the Mesopotamian ziggurat's role in religious life and ritual; parallels between the building of ziggurats and the story of the Tower of Babel.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E03 — The Journeys of Abraham
Tracing the life of Abraham from his origins; how Abraham follows the call of God in traveling to Canaan; historical evidence related to the events of Abraham's journey; the narrative of Abraham's search for an heir to his clan and to God's covenant.

title: The History and Archaeology of the Bible
description:
S01 E04 — Joseph in Egypt
Archeological traces of Abraham's descendants; the events surrounding Dinah, daughter of Jacob; how their clan is forced to leave Canaan; the story of Joseph's bondage in Egypt; the plausibility of Joseph's rise to the grand vizier to the Pharaoh.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E01 — A Middle East Crossroads in the Year 1900
How western imperialism, the politics of oil, and the push for a Jewish state all set the stage for the 20th century.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E02 — Constitutional Revolts in Persia and Turkey
How protests in Persia led to a new government; then why the Young Turks wanted a united Turkey to supersede the Ottoman Empire.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E03 — World War I and the Ottoman Empire's Fall
The promises of Arab and Turkish nationalism and the construction of a Jewish state collide after the war.

title: The Middle East in the 20th Century
description:
S01 E04 — Egyptian Revolution and Turkish Independence
The fallout from World War I with a look at the Turkish War of Independence in 1919, as well as anti-British uprisings from Egypt to Iraq.

title: Books that Matter: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
description:
S01 E01 — The Greatness of Gibbon's Decline and Fall
Grounding one's understanding of Gibbon's masterpiece; why Rome is so important to Gibbon and his readers; what makes the periodic style so essential to the book's accessibility; why people should want to read it in the 21st century.

title: Books that Matter: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
description:
S01 E02 — The Making of Gibbon the Historian
Following Edward Gibbon's intellectual development; exploring his childhood obsession with reading, his military service, his disappointed love, his social circles, his personal politics, and his life as a gentleman scholar of leisure.

title: Books that Matter: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
description:
S01 E03 — The Empire at Its Beginning
Professor Damrosch reviews early Roman history; exploring the empire's important provinces, the excessive influence of the Roman military, the emergence of imperial dictatorship, and other facts Gibbon's original readers took for granted.

title: Books that Matter: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
description:
S01 E04 — The Theory and Practice of History
Exploring Gibbon's understanding of the role of the historian; discovering his thoughts about Hume, Voltaire, and other enlightenment writers; learning how he revolutionizes the use of extensive documentation in his work.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E01 — The Christian Conquest of Rome
An overview of Christianity, the role of Jesus's earliest followers, and a few theories to explain how it became the most widely practiced religion in the world.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E02 — Pagan Religions in the Roman World
Insight into the significance of paganism, a complex term used in the pre-Christian Roman Empire to refer to the polytheistic religions that were widely followed at the time.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E03 — Judaism in the Roman World
Insight into the significance of Judaism, an ancient monotheistic religion that was initially practiced by many, including Jesus and his early followers.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Christianity in the Roam World: An Overview
Christianity's success stems from its similarities to and differences from other religious practices.
